docs.title: Booknook
docs.text: A self-hosted personal library server for ebooks and comics. Runs on Bun with Hono, SQLite, and a plugin system for extending functionality.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Ebooks — upload and read EPUB/PDF files with a full in-browser reader powered by foliate-js
  • Comics — upload CBZ/CBR files; series and issues are auto-grouped from ComicInfo.xml metadata
  • Multi-user — session-based auth with per-user reading progress; admin panel for user management
  • Plugin system — drop a folder into plugins/ to add new routes, nav items, and lifecycle hooks
  • Docker-ready — single docker compose up for production deployment

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
bun install
cp .env.example .env   # edit as needed
bun run dev

Open http://localhost:3001.

See Getting Started for a full walkthrough.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: All configuration is done via environment variables, typically in a .env file.

docs.title: Core
docs.text: Variable Required Default Description SESSION_SECRET no dev-secret Secret used to sign session cookies. Set a strong random value in production. PORT no 3001 Port the server listens on. NODE_ENV no — Set to production to disable the livereload overlay.

docs.title: Admin bootstrap
docs.text:
These are only read at startup. If the named user doesn't exist yet, it is created with admin privileges.

Variable Required Description ADMIN_USERNAME no Username for the auto-created admin account. ADMIN_PASSWORD no Password for the auto-created admin account.

docs.title: Plugin variables
docs.text: Variable Used by Description GEMINI_API_KEY ai-integration Google Gemini API key for AI book recommendations. GOOGLE_BOOKS_API_KEY core Improves cover art fetch quality via the Google Books API. ANNAS_SECRET_KEY annas-archive Anna's Archive API key for search and download. ANNAS_BASE_URL annas-archive Override the default Anna's Archive mirror URL.

docs.title: Example .env
docs.text:
SESSION_SECRET=change-me-to-something-random
ADMIN_USERNAME=admin
ADMIN_PASSWORD=changeme

# Optional: better cover images
GOOGLE_BOOKS_API_KEY=

# Optional: AI recommendations
GEMINI_API_KEY=

docs.title: Database Schema
docs.text: Booknook uses a single SQLite file (booknook.db) managed by bun:sqlite. All tables are created with CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so the schema is applied automatically on first run and is safe to re-run on restart.

docs.title: users
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
    id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    username      TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    password_hash TEXT NOT NULL,
    is_admin      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    created_at    TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

Passwords are hashed with bcrypt (cost 10). is_admin = 1 grants access to /admin/* routes.

docs.title: books
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS books (
    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    title      TEXT NOT NULL,
    author     TEXT,
    isbn       TEXT UNIQUE,
    filePath   TEXT UNIQUE,
    status     TEXT DEFAULT 'none',
    created_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

status is one of none, want, reading, read.

docs.title: reading_progress
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS reading_progress (
    user_id    INTEGER NOT NULL,
    book_id    INTEGER NOT NULL,
    cfi        TEXT,
    percentage REAL DEFAULT 0,
    updated_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP,
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, book_id)
);

cfi is an EPUB CFI string used by foliate-js to restore the exact reading position.

docs.title: comics
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS comics (
    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    title      TEXT NOT NULL,
    series     TEXT,
    issue      TEXT,
    filePath   TEXT UNIQUE,
    pageCount  INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    status     TEXT DEFAULT 'none',
    created_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

series and issue are populated from ComicInfo.xml when present.

docs.title: comic_progress
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS comic_progress (
    user_id    INTEGER NOT NULL,
    comic_id   INTEGER NOT NULL,
    page       INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, comic_id)
);

docs.title: sessions
docs.text:
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS sessions (
    id         TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    data       TEXT NOT NULL,
    expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL
);

Used by the session middleware to persist login state across restarts.

docs.title: Plugin tables
docs.text: Plugins create their own tables using CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS inside their register() function. By convention, table names are prefixed with the plugin name (e.g. ai_integration, myplugin_items).

docs.title: Docker Compose (recommended)
docs.text:
The included docker-compose.yml builds the image and mounts persistent volumes for user data.

docker compose up -d

docs.title: Persistent volumes
docs.text: Host path Container path Purpose ./books /app/books Uploaded EPUB/PDF files ./comics /app/comics Uploaded CBZ/CBR files ./cache /app/cache Extracted cover images ./booknook.db /app/booknook.db SQLite database

docs.title: Environment
docs.text:
Copy .env.example to .env and set at minimum:

SESSION_SECRET=<random-string>
ADMIN_USERNAME=admin
ADMIN_PASSWORD=<strong-password>

The docker-compose.yml reads .env automatically via env_file.

docs.title: Building the image manually
docs.text:
docker build -t booknook .
docker run -p 3001:3001 --env-file .env \
  -v ./books:/app/books \
  -v ./comics:/app/comics \
  -v ./cache:/app/cache \
  -v ./booknook.db:/app/booknook.db \
  booknook

docs.title: System dependencies (non-Docker)
docs.text:
The Dockerfile documents the exact packages needed. For a bare-metal install:

Package Purpose imagemagick Cover image resizing (magick / convert) poppler-utils PDF cover extraction (pdftoppm) python3, python3-venv comic-dl plugin chromium comic-dl headless browser xz-utils annas-archive binary extraction

docs.title: Reverse proxy
docs.text:
Booknook itself does not handle TLS. Put it behind nginx or Caddy in production.

Minimal Caddy example:

your.domain {
    reverse_proxy localhost:3001
}

docs.title: Updating
docs.text:
git pull
docker compose build
docker compose up -d

The database schema is managed by database.ts using CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, so updates are non-destructive.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Bun v1.0 or later
  • imagemagick — for cover image resizing (magick / convert)
  • poppler-utils — for PDF cover extraction (pdftoppm)

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
git clone <repo-url>
cd booknook
bun install

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Copy the example env file and fill in the values you need:

cp .env.example .env

At minimum, set SESSION_SECRET for any non-development use. See Configuration for all options.

docs.title: Running
docs.text:
DevelopmentProductionDocker 
bun run dev

Hot-reloads on file changes via a livereload websocket injected automatically in dev mode.

bun run start

docker compose up -d

See Deployment for details.

The server listens on port 3001 by default (override with PORT=).

docs.title: First login
docs.text: On first start, if ADMIN_USERNAME and ADMIN_PASSWORD are set in .env, that admin account is created automatically. Otherwise, create the first user by inserting directly into the database or via the /admin/users panel once you have an account.

docs.title: Directory layout
docs.text:
app.ts            — Hono server and all core routes
database.ts       — bun:sqlite setup and schema migrations
plugins/          — plugin registry + one subdirectory per plugin
middleware/       — auth, session, dev livereload
utils/            — EPUB/CBZ parsing, cover fetching, metadata lookup
views/            — Pug templates (layout.pug is the shared shell)
public/           — static assets (foliate-js reader, CSS, icons)
books/            — uploaded EPUB/PDF files (git-ignored)
comics/           — uploaded CBZ/CBR files (git-ignored)
cache/covers/     — extracted cover images (git-ignored)

docs.title: Supported formats
docs.text: Format Notes .epub Native — metadata and cover extracted directly .pdf Converted to EPUB at upload time; cover extracted from first page .mobi, .azw, .azw3 Accepted but not converted .djvu, .fb2 Accepted but not converted

docs.title: Uploading
docs.text:
Drag and drop one or more files onto the library page, or use the upload button. Multiple files are processed in parallel. Duplicate files (same path) are silently skipped.

On upload, Booknook:

  1. Saves the file to books/
  2. Extracts title, author, and ISBN from the file metadata
  3. For PDFs: looks up metadata by filename via the Google Books API
  4. Normalises to EPUB where possible
  5. Fetches and caches a cover image (from the file or Google Books)

docs.title: Reading
docs.text: Click any book to open the in-browser reader, powered by foliate-js. Reading position (CFI + percentage) is saved automatically per-user as you read.

docs.title: Reading status
docs.text:
Right-click a book (or use the context menu) to set a status:

Status Meaning none Default / unset want Want to read reading Currently reading read Finished

docs.title: API endpoints
docs.text: Method Path Description GET / Library home — lists all books POST /upload Upload one or more book files (multipart uploadedBook) GET /reader/:id Open the in-browser reader GET /books/spine/:id JSON spine for a book GET /books/stream/:id/* Stream a resource (chapter, image) from inside an EPUB GET /books/file/:id Download the raw book file POST /books/:id/progress Save reading progress { cfi, percentage } PATCH /books/:id/status Update reading status { status } DELETE /books/:id Delete a book and its cover

docs.title: Supported formats
docs.text: Format Notes .cbz ZIP archive of images — fully supported .cbr RAR archive of images — fully supported

docs.title: Uploading
docs.text:
Use the upload button on the /comics page. On upload, Booknook:

  1. Saves the file to comics/
  2. Parses ComicInfo.xml from inside the archive (if present) to extract title, series, and issue number
  3. Falls back to the filename if no ComicInfo.xml is found
  4. Extracts the first image as a cover and saves it to cache/covers/

docs.title: Series grouping
docs.text: Comics with the same series value from ComicInfo.xml are automatically grouped on the library page. Issues are sorted numerically; specials (non-numeric issue values) are sorted alphabetically and placed after numbered issues.

docs.title: Reading
docs.text: Click a comic to open the page-by-page reader. Page position is saved automatically per-user.

docs.title: Reading status
docs.text: Same statuses as books: none, want, reading, read.

docs.title: ComicInfo.xml
docs.text:
Booknook reads the following fields from ComicInfo.xml:

Field Used for <Title> Comic title <Series> Series grouping <Number> Issue number

docs.title: API endpoints
docs.text: Method Path Description GET /comics Comics library page POST /comics/upload Upload a CBZ/CBR file (multipart comic) GET /comics/read/:id Open the comic reader GET /comics/pages/:id JSON list of page filenames in the archive GET /comics/page/:id/* Stream a single page image POST /comics/:id/progress Save page position { page } PATCH /comics/:id/status Update reading status { status } DELETE /comics/:id Delete a comic and its cover

docs.title: AI Integration Plugin
docs.text: The ai-integration plugin adds AI-powered book recommendations using Google Gemini.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
Set GEMINI_API_KEY in your .env:

GEMINI_API_KEY=your-key-here

Without this key the plugin loads but the recommendation feature is disabled and shows a configuration notice in the UI.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
1. Navigate to AI in the sidebar.
  2. Select a book from your library.
  3. Click Get Recommendations — Gemini returns five books with a short reason for each.
  4. Recommendations are saved per-book and displayed on revisit.

Generating new recommendations for a book replaces the previously stored ones.

docs.title: Rate limits
docs.text: The plugin uses the free Gemini tier by default. If you hit the quota, the UI displays a friendly message with a retry countdown when available.

docs.title: Routes
docs.text:
All routes are under /plugins/ai-integration.

Method Path Description GET / Recommendations dashboard GET /api/book/:id Fetch book metadata as JSON POST /api/recommendations/:id Generate (and store) recommendations for a book

docs.title: Database
docs.text:
The plugin creates one table:

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS ai_integration (
    id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    book_id    INTEGER NOT NULL,
    note       TEXT    NOT NULL,   -- JSON array of recommendations
    created_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

On bookDeleted, the plugin cleans up its rows automatically.

docs.title: Plugin System
docs.text: Booknook has a first-class plugin system. Plugins are loaded at startup from subdirectories of plugins/ and can add routes, nav items, stylesheets, scripts, and lifecycle event listeners.

docs.title: How plugins are loaded
docs.text:
At startup, plugins/index.ts scans plugins/ for subdirectories. Any folder that contains a plugin.ts or plugin.js is loaded (the example/ folder is always skipped). Each plugin's register() function is called with a context object that gives it access to the database, router, and extension hooks.

If a plugin's register() throws, it is skipped and the rest of the app continues normally.

docs.title: Bundled plugins
docs.text: Plugin Description ai-integration AI-powered book recommendations via Google Gemini

docs.title: Writing your own
docs.text: See Writing a Plugin for a full guide, and plugins/example/ for a minimal working reference that demonstrates every hook.

docs.title: Writing a Plugin
docs.text: Plugins live in plugins/<name>/ and are loaded automatically at startup.

docs.title: File structure
docs.text:
plugins/
  my-plugin/
    plugin.ts        ← required (or plugin.js)
    views/           ← optional Pug templates
    public/          ← optional static assets (CSS, JS, images)

docs.title: Minimal plugin
docs.text:
plugin.ts must export a default object with a name and a register function:

import type { PluginContext } from '../index';

export default {
    name: 'my-plugin',
    version: '1.0.0',

    register({ db, router, pluginDir, render, addNavItem, addStylesheet, addScript, on }: PluginContext) {
        // your plugin code here
    },
};

docs.title: db
docs.text:
A bun:sqlite Database instance connected to the main booknook.db.

db.prepare('CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS myplugin_items (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT)').run();
const rows = db.prepare('SELECT * FROM myplugin_items').all();

Always prefix your table names to avoid collisions. Use CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS so they survive restarts.

docs.title: router
docs.text:
A Hono router automatically mounted at /plugins/<folder-name>. Add your routes here.

router.get('/', c => {
    return render(c, path.join(pluginDir, 'views/index.pug'), { items: [] });
});

router.post('/api/thing', async c => {
    const body = await c.req.json();
    return c.json({ ok: true }, 201);
});

docs.title: render(c, templatePath, locals?)
docs.text:
Renders a Pug template with the standard layout variables pre-populated (user, currentPath, plugin nav items, etc.).

return render(c, path.join(pluginDir, 'views/page.pug'), { data });

Always use the absolute pluginDir-based path — relative paths won't resolve from inside the registry.

docs.title: pluginDir
docs.text: Absolute path to your plugin folder.

docs.title: addNavItem(item)
docs.text:
Adds a link to the sidebar navigation.

addNavItem({
    label: 'My Plugin',
    href: '/plugins/my-plugin',
    icon: `<svg width="18" height="18" .../>`,  // optional inline SVG
});

docs.title: addStylesheet(href) / addScript(src)
docs.text:
Injects a <link> or <script> tag into every page. Serve files from public/ — they're automatically mounted at /plugins/<name>/.

addStylesheet('/plugins/my-plugin/styles.css');
addScript('/plugins/my-plugin/client.js');

docs.title: on(event, handler)
docs.text:
Subscribe to lifecycle events emitted by the core app.

on('bookDeleted', ({ id, book }) => {
    db.prepare('DELETE FROM myplugin_items WHERE book_id = ?').run(id);
});

docs.title: Available events
docs.text: Event Payload Fired when bookDeleted { id: number, book: object } A book is removed from the library bookUploaded { id, title, author, isbn, filePath } A book is successfully uploaded and registered

docs.title: Static assets
docs.text: Files in public/ are served at /plugins/<name>/ automatically. They are also available at /plugins/<name>/static/ as an alias.

docs.title: Tips
docs.text:
• Prefix all DB table names: myplugin_notes, not notes.
  • Errors thrown from register() are caught and logged — your plugin is skipped, but the app keeps running.
  • If your plugin needs an external process or binary, start setup in register() so it's ready by the first request. Use a flag to avoid re-running setup on every call.
